raw_response:
I'll think through this year's planning as this farmer would.

**My reasoning:**

I've been farming these 5 mu for 50 years, same wheat-maize rotation like everyone in Quzhou. My middle school education helped me read fertilizer bags and listen to the agro-tech station people when they come, but mostly I do what worked last year and what my neighbors do. With 7 people in the household and some working outside, money from off-farm helps, but I still count every yuan on inputs.

**Winter wheat (already in ground from last October, but planning for this cycle):**
Last year I used about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, 50 kg each) as base before planting — that's 100 kg total on 5 mu, so 20 kg/mu. Then I top-dress with urea at jointing in spring, about 15 kg urea per mu (that's about 7 kg N). So total N is around 17-18 kg/mu. I'll do the same this year — no reason to change, wheat did 450 kg/mu last year which is normal around here.

I irrigate wheat 3 times: before winter (dong shui), at green-up/jointing in spring, and at grain-filling. The well is reliable. I spray pesticide twice — once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading, and herbicide once in spring. I use improved variety seed from the town dealer, Jimai or Shiluan type, everyone plants these.

**Summer maize (plant in June after wheat harvest):**
I'll plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever the dealer has fresh. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat. I use 1 bag compound (50 kg) as base before planting and then side-dress urea at big trumpet stage, about 20 kg urea per mu. Total N comes to about 16-17 kg/mu. Phosphorus and potassium mainly from the base compound.

Summer rain usually covers maize, but July-August can be dry so I irrigate once or twice from the well. Spray once for corn borer. No tillage for maize — I just plant directly into wheat stubble with the seeder, saves money and time. Wheat I still rotary till before planting in autumn.

Yield targets: wheat 450 kg/mu, maize 550 kg/mu — normal for our land.
